title: The Seagull and the Crab
logline: An old seabird too weak to hunt tricks the fish of his pond into letting him carry them, two a day, to a safe pond that does not exist; when the crab takes his turn and sees the bones, he seizes the bird by the neck and ends it.
moral: Do not hand yourself to an old enemy because he sounds kind; and the trickster who lives by deceit is finished by the first victim who sees clearly and acts.
tone: A dark comic fable played straight: gentle and sunny at the pond, a cold turn at the hill, a tense silent climax, and a quiet, relieved ending. Violence is shown by gulps, clean skeletons and cartoon crosses, never by blood.

beats.summary: An old bird beside a pond full of fish (twelve, counted on screen).
Once he fished with ease; now he is old, weak and misses.
The crab, friend of the fish, comes by and asks why he is sad.
The lie: two fishermen will return and take every fish.
The crab spreads the news; the fish panic and go to the bird for advice.
The offer: a far, safe pond, and he will carry them.
Two fish a day leave in his beak; the others wave.
There is no new pond: a rocky hill where he eats them.
The crab asks to go too; the bird takes him in his claws.
In the air the crab searches the ground for water and finds none.
Fish bones on the stones: eight, the number that left.
He understands his friends were eaten and that he is next.
He clamps both pincers on the bird neck.
He squeezes until the bird dies; both fall near the pond.
The surviving fish learn the truth.
The bird no longer appears each morning; the pond is safe.

cast.name: the old seabird
cast.look: Big white gull-like water bird about 300 units tall standing: grey wings with black tips, long S-shaped neck, long yellow hooked beak with a red spot, yellow legs with three clawed toes. Old: grey brow feather, ragged wing and tail feathers, stoop. Gets a rounder belly after Day 4.

cast.name: the crab
cast.look: Red round-shelled crab, shell 150 x 96 units, cream belly, two eye stalks, six walking legs, two big pincers that can reach above his eyes. Drawn at s 0.8 beside the bird.

cast.name: the fish of the pond
cast.look: Twelve fish: four sleek yellow, four red with white bellies, four round pink. Two are featured: the smallest yellow one and a round pink one. Four survive (one of each palette plus the smallest red).

cast.name: two fishermen (inside the thought cloud only)
cast.base: person kind:'owner' as planned villager variants, one tall and one short
cast.look: Small figures (about 110 px on screen) with a hand net and a big net; never appear in the real world.

sets.description: Split-level pond (planned name pond, with a cutaway option). World 1000 x 1230. Sky with hillTrees horizon at y 520. Left bank top at y 600 from x 0 to 330; the bank slopes under water through (430,820) and (600,1040) to a bed at y 1060..1090. Water surface y 640 from x 345 to the right edge. Reeds at x 372..410 and 930..990; weed tufts on the bed; a flat stone at (700,1062). Sky preset parameter (day, dawn, dusk) and dayCycle. Positions approximate until drawn; the animator fixes them once and keeps them.

Barren grey hill, new. World 1000 x 1230, dusk sky. Flat ledge at y 780 from x 300 to 760; a spire on the right from (760,780) up to (900,420); left slope falls to (0,1080); boulders in the foreground below y 1000; a bare dead trunk at (700,780), 150 tall; a dry cracked hollow at (400,770). Bones layer: n skeletons at fixed seeded positions along x 340..720.

Library sky with two parallax layers of cloudFlat and the planned aerialStrip along y 1000..1230 (dry fields, stones, thorn bushes; no water). The sky blends from the day preset to dusk between 109 and 112.8.

props.description: Clean fish skeleton, 90 x 34 units: triangular skull with an eye hole, spine line, six rib pairs, tail fan; white with a black brush outline. shape parameter (slim, round, small) so two can echo the featured fish; also used as a 40 px icon.
White feather 46 x 14 with a grey quill, drifts on swing() and lies on the ground.

ending.description: Morning at the pond, wide. The bank is empty except for a feather; the crab stands guard where the bird used to sit; four fish swim easily and the smallest leaps. THE END stamps into the sky at 174.6 and holds to 177.44 with only blinks, ripples and slow fish loops.

subtitles.ar: كان طائر كبير يعيش قرب بركة مليئة بالسمك.|عاش سنوات طويلة يصطاد فيها بسهولة، لكنه كبر وضعف جسمه.|وفي يوم، جلس قرب الماء حزينًا|لأنه لم يعد يستطيع الصيد كما كان.
subtitles.en: An old bird lived beside a pond full of fish.|For many years he caught fish easily, but he grew old and weak.|One day he sat sadly by the water|because he could no longer hunt as before.

subtitles.ar: مر به سرطان يعيش في البركة، وسأله: «لماذا تبدو حزينًا؟»|قال الطائر: «سمعت صيادين يقولان إنهما سيعودان قريبًا|ليأخذا كل السمك من هنا.|أخاف أن تصبح البركة خالية.»
subtitles.en: A crab living in the pond passed and asked, “Why do you look so sad?”|The bird said, “I heard two fishermen say they will return soon|and take every fish from here.|I fear the pond will be empty.”

subtitles.ar: أسرع السرطان إلى السمك وأخبره بما سمع.|خافت الأسماك واجتمعت حول الطائر تطلب النصيحة.|قال لها: «أعرف بركة أخرى بعيدة،|فيها ماء كثير ولا يأتي إليها الصيادون. أستطيع أن أنقلكن إليها.»
subtitles.en: The crab hurried to the fish and told them what he had heard.|The fish were frightened and gathered around the bird for advice.|He said, “I know another pond far away,|with plenty of water and no fishermen. I can carry you there.”

subtitles.ar: وافقت الأسماك، فصار الطائر يحمل سمكتين كل يوم ويطير بهما بعيدًا.|لكن لم تكن هناك بركة جديدة.|كان يهبط فوق تل صخري، ويأكل السمكتين،|ثم يعود ليأخذ غيرهما.
subtitles.en: The fish agreed, so every day the bird carried two fish away.|But there was no new pond.|He landed on a rocky hill, ate both fish,|then returned to take more.

subtitles.ar: بعد أيام، قال السرطان: «أنا أيضًا أريد الذهاب إلى البركة الآمنة.»|وافق الطائر وحمله بين مخالبه.|ارتفعا في السماء، وبدأ السرطان ينظر إلى الأرض|بحثًا عن الماء الذي وعد به الطائر.
subtitles.en: After several days the crab said, “I too want to go to the safe pond.”|The bird agreed and carried him in his claws.|As they flew, the crab searched the ground|for the water the bird had promised.

subtitles.ar: اقتربا من التل الصخري،|فرأى السرطان عظام أسماك كثيرة منتشرة فوق الحجارة.|فهم الحقيقة فورًا: الطائر لم ينقذ أصدقاءه، بل أكلهم جميعًا.|وعرف أنه سيكون الضحية التالية.
subtitles.en: They approached the rocky hill,|and the crab saw many fish bones scattered across the stones.|He understood at once: the bird had not rescued his friends but eaten them.|He knew he was next.

subtitles.ar: قبل أن يهبط الطائر، رفع السرطان كلبتيه القويتين وأمسك بعنقه.|حاول الطائر أن يفلت،|لكن السرطان ضغط بكل قوته حتى مات الطائر،|وسقط الاثنان قرب البركة.
subtitles.en: Before the bird could land, the crab raised his strong pincers and gripped the bird’s neck.|The bird tried to escape,|but the crab squeezed with all his strength until the bird died.|They both fell near the pond.

subtitles.ar: عاد السرطان إلى الماء، وأخبر الأسماك الباقية بما حدث.|عرفت أن أصدقاءها لم يصلوا إلى بركة آمنة قط.|ولم يعد الطائر يظهر كل صباح ليأخذ اثنتين أخريين.
subtitles.en: The crab returned to the water and told the surviving fish what had happened.|They learned that their friends had never reached a safe pond.|And the bird no longer appeared each morning to carry away two more.

new_assets.name: waterBird
new_assets.description: Large wading or sea bird (kinds gull, later heron, pelican, stork) for pond and shore fables. Standing 300 tall x 260 wide at s 1, feet at (x,y). Fields: age 0..1, belly 0..1, neck 0..1, headRot, beak 0..1, talk, brow, eyes (open, wide, x), ph/amp (two-leg walk), sit 0..1, fly + flap (wingspan 420), wing -1..1 (near wing as an arm), wingsUp 0..1, hold (fish, fish2), gulp 0..1 (bulge position along the neck), feet (open, grip), choke 0..1 with chokeAt (pinch point on the neck), limp 0..1, plus the shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: One function in Library/cast. Body: ellipse 190 x 120, white, blue Ben-Day dots on the underside. Neck: a quadratic curve of length 120 drawn as a 30 px white stroke over a 38 px black stroke, control point from neck and headRot; gulp draws a circle r 22 along the curve; choke narrows the stroke to 14 px at chokeAt and enlarges the head 8 %. Head: circle r 34 with helpers eye2 (gaze, lid, wet). Beak: two tapered polygons 86 long, lower one rotates up to 0.6 rad; red dot near the tip. Wings: folded = one grey teardrop on the body; flying = two-segment polygons driven by flap. Legs: two-segment yellow strokes 110 long with three toes; grip curls the toes round a 120-wide object and exposes the grip point (x + 10*dir, y + 95*s in flight). age blends posture, a grey brow bar and three notches in wing and tail. Wrap with acting().

new_assets.name: crab
new_assets.description: Red crab for water fables. Shell 150 x 96 at s 1, total about 260 wide with pincers and 140 tall with stalks. Fields: ph/amp (six-leg scuttle), stalk 0..1.3 (stalk length), stalkLean -1..1, pinL/pinR (pincer targets in figure space, with arm IK), openL/openR 0..1, talk, mouth (closed, smile, frown, o), brow, eyes (open, wide), tuck 0..1 (legs drawn in), dangle 0..1 (legs hang), plus the shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: Shell: ellipse with the flat process red, red-dot shading below, cream belly arc, black brush outline. Stalks: two 34-unit strokes from (+-26, -48) ending in eyeballs r 15 drawn with eye2. Legs: three per side, two-segment tapered strokes, alternating tripod phase from ph. Pincer arms: two segments of 52 each solved with the same IK as armTo in core/helpers.js; pincer = fixed upper finger 62 x 26 plus a hinged thumb rotating by open * 0.7 rad. Wrap with acting().

new_assets.name: fish
new_assets.description: The planned side-view fish (KD-007): palettes 0 sleek yellow, 1 red with white belly, 2 round pink; fields ph, amp, bend, rot, roll, talk, plus acting fields. This story also needs s down to 0.6 for the smallest fish and a head-up pose at the surface (rot -1.2).
new_assets.implementation: As specified by KD-007. Body 110 x 50 ellipse with tail fan and one eye (eye2). If KD-007 has not been built yet, build it here to that specification and register it.

new_assets.name: pond
new_assets.description: The planned pond set with a cutaway option: bank, water surface, underwater bowl and bed in one 1000 x 1230 world (dimensions in sets). level parameter kept at 1 here.
new_assets.implementation: Bake sky + hillTrees + bank and bed polygons (ground colours with dots). Water: a blue polygon under the surface line at alpha 0.85 with lighter dot bands, drawn after the bed and before the characters that are under water; a white surface line with a 3 px sine ripple drawn last, so figures crossing the surface are tinted below it by re-drawing the water at alpha 0.35 over them, clipped below y 640.

new_assets.name: rockyHill
new_assets.description: Barren rock hill with a landing ledge and a bones layer (dimensions in sets). Reusable for any lair, cliff or mountain top.
new_assets.implementation: Three grey polygons (far spire, main mass, foreground boulders) with grey dot shading and crack lines like the Library den rock; ledge edge as a fat brush line; bones drawn from a seeded list of {x, y, rot, shape} so the count can grow 2, 4, 6, 8.

new_assets.name: fishBones
new_assets.description: Fish skeleton prop and icon (see props).
new_assets.implementation: Polygon skull, one line spine, six short rib strokes each side scaled by a shape profile, tail fan of three strokes; white fill, black outline.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: The planned generic thought cloud, used five times (the lie, the promise, the crab wish, the truth, the telling). Box up to 560 x 340 with a tail of three puffs to the thinker.
new_assets.implementation: Cloud outline from overlapping circles, white fill; contents drawn through a callback inside a clip, scaled so figures are at least 110 px on screen.

new_assets.name: dayCycle
new_assets.description: The planned sky that runs through day, dusk, night and dawn; here for the fast years at 6.46, the DAY tags and the last morning.
new_assets.implementation: Blend the Library sky presets by a phase value and move sun() along an arc.

new_assets.name: splash
new_assets.description: The planned splash crown, rings and bubble trail for everything that crosses the surface.
new_assets.implementation: As planned by KD-007: six to eight drops on short arcs plus two expanding ellipses on the surface line.

new_assets.name: aerialStrip
new_assets.description: The planned scrolling ground seen from the air, here with a dry palette and no water.
new_assets.implementation: Three tiled bands scrolling at different speeds from the flight distance function.

new_assets.name: swimPath
new_assets.description: The planned fish motion from keyed 2D paths, with a per-fish delay so the school never moves in unison.
new_assets.implementation: kfn on x and y, direction and tail phase from the distance travelled (as swimPhase does for the turtle).

new_assets.name: carryRig
new_assets.description: Rider follows a carrier grip point with a damped swing and a lag; used both ways here: crab in the bird feet, then crab hanging from the bird neck. A small case of the planned carryRig and of rideOn from the guide wish list.
new_assets.implementation: rider position = carrier grip point; rider tip = swing() driven by the carrier acceleration, sampled 2 frames late; all a pure function of t.

owner_questions: The title says seagull but the Arabic only says a big bird: I drew him as a big gull-like water bird with a long neck (default); a heron look is the alternative.
Eating is softened: two gulps shown as bulges in the neck, then clean skeletons drawn from the beak, no blood (default).
The death is softened: crosses for eyes, limp wings, a fall and a dust cloud; the body lies on the bank for about three seconds and is gone by the last morning, leaving one feather (default).
The script says a pond full of fish and several days; I fixed the numbers at twelve fish, two a day for four days, eight skeletons and four survivors, shown by FISH, DAY and BONES counters (default).
The fish hop into his beak of their own will and travel there, while the crab is carried in the claws as the script says (default).
A mask slip of 0.4 s at 43.3 s hints that the bird is lying before the narrator says so at 77 s (default: keep it, very small).
Invented English lettering: YEARS AGO, NOW, EEK!, YES! YES!, NO POND!, GULP!, DAYS LATER..., BONES!, NEXT!, SNAP!, THUD! plus the title and THE END (default: all kept).
Additions at the end that are not in the script: the crab takes the bird place on the bank as a guard and the smallest fish leaps (default: kept).
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; cue every action with w(p, n) from timing.json. The cue words and times in this file are the starts on the final MP3.

Word ends in the timeline run up to the next word, so only the listed gaps are free for effects: 5.12-5.78, 13.52-14.24, 21.80-22.80, 26.46-27.02, 43.14-43.88, 76.86-77.22, 88.72-89.80, 96.90-97.94, 127.08-127.48, 133.26-133.94, 157.60-158.42 and after 173.84. SNAP! (140.56) and THUD! (152.3) are therefore silent picture hits: flash, panel-only shake and lettering, no sound.
Set LIFE.t = t every frame so all figures blink; use P.noBlink for the crab from 115.24 to 116.7 and for the dead bird.

One fish list of twelve {id, pal, s, seed}; fish 0 is the smallest yellow (s 0.6), fish 8 the round pink. Days remove pairs (0,8), (1,5), (2,9), (4,10); survivors 3, 6, 7, 11. Every scene draws the fish from this list so the counter and the picture always agree.
Counters live in panel space at the top corners of the picture (DAY left, FISH or BONES right), drawn after the world and before finish; hide them in S3 to S7 and S11, S13 to S15.
Under water, tint figures by re-drawing the water at alpha 0.35 over them; draw order: baked set, bed props, fish and crab below the surface, water tint, surface line, bank figures, reeds.
Flight: positions from keyed paths (kfn); flap phase from the distance flown; the rider (fish tails, crab) takes its position from the carrier grip point with swing() two frames late.
The grip: at 140.56 the crab pincer targets are the two sides of the neck at chokeAt 0.55; from 141.52 the carrier relation inverts (crab position = neck point, body hanging below).
Camera cuts between sets are hard cuts on the scene boundaries except 88.9 (card), 151.9 (hidden in the fall) and 168.02 (0.4 s dissolve through the dayCycle).
Thought clouds must never cover a face; keep them in the upper right and keep the figures inside at 110 px or more on screen.

Subtitles: Noto Naskh Arabic 700 with the chunks given here; two chunks are long (P3 chunk 4, P7 chunk 1), so let the caption panel wrap them onto three lines rather than shrink the type below the standard size.
When the new figures are approved, move waterBird, crab, fish, pond, rockyHill and fishBones into Library with registry entries, then run node Library/tests/regression.mjs.
warnings: Three new figures (waterBird, crab, fish) carry the whole film; the waterBird neck (curl, gulp, choke, limp) is the largest piece of new drawing and should be tested in stills first.
The climax has no room for sound effects because the narration has no pause between 133.94 and 154.42; it must read in pictures alone.
The grip pose must be readable at phone size: both pincers clearly on either side of a long neck against plain sky, never against the grey rock.
The fish and pond drawings are planned by KD-007 and KD-008/KD-012; if those stories are built first, reuse their code instead of drawing again.
The counters invent exact numbers the script does not state; see owner questions.
